1.pericope_label: The word of the Lord which came unto Zephaniah
debates: Whether the Hizkiah of the pedigree is king Hezekiah
Whether the prophecy falls before or after the reformation of Josiah
Why innocent creatures are swept away with guilty men
What the stumblingblocks are
outliers: Calvin denies the rule that a prophet who names his father must himself be son of a prophet, and reads the name of Amon as reproach rather than honour
Ellicott refuses for this word the sense of a ruin that it bears elsewhere, and takes it for the enticements to sin
themes: A pedigree carried back to a king
A sentence pronounced without preamble
The gathering that empties a land
Fowl and fish drawn into a human quarrel

4.pericope_label: I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem
debates: What the remnant of Baal implies about Josiah reformation
Whether the priests named with the Chemarims are idol priests or lawful priests who connived
Where the name Chemarim comes from
Whether the idolaters could plead ignorance
outliers: Ellicott takes the name Malcham for a blend of their king with Moloch and reports a guess that identifies the deity with the planet Saturn
Calvin explains a remnant surviving a thorough purge by private worship kept up at home under fear of men
themes: A hand stretched out rather than merely moved
A holy city certain it is the exception
Black-robed priests whose very name is to go
Roofs climbed to be nearer the stars

7.pericope_label: Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is at hand
debates: Who the bidden guests are
What the commanded silence means
In what sense a judgment is a sacrifice
outliers: Wesley makes the guests the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air rather than the invading nations
Calvin turns the silence into a general disposition, submission set against a contumacy that is always clamorous
themes: A word that is only a hush
A Father present as a Judge
Men slain as fast as lambs for the altar
Invited ones consecrated to a banquet

8.pericope_label: I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel
debates: Who the king children are
Whether strange apparel means foreign dress or foreign customs
What leaping on the threshold describes
Whose house is filled with violence and deceit
outliers: Ellicott rejects the sons of Josiah on chronological grounds and reads the king brothers or uncles instead
Clarke reports a reading drawn from riders who forced their way into houses to plunder, which he says is why doors in parts of the East are made low
themes: Three ranks named so that none may plead exemption
A fringe meant to be looked at and remembered
A threshold too holy to be trodden on
A temple filled with what fraud brought in

10.pericope_label: there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and an howling from the second
debates: What the second names
Whether Maktesh is a proper name or a description of a hollow quarter
What the hills are
Why the traders are called the people of Canaan
outliers: Calvin denies that Maktesh is a proper name and derives the sense of pounding from the shape of the hollow rather than the reverse
Wesley alone hears in the crashing the noise of doors and chests broken open
themes: A ruin set before the eyes as a scene
Three quarters chosen so no corner stays quiet
A hollow named for a mortar
Men laden with the silver they came to spend

12.pericope_label: I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees
debates: How a searching with candles agrees with omniscience
Whether the men on their lees are merely the secure rich or open despisers of God
What settling on the lees pictures
outliers: Clarke gives the practical atheism of these men a philosophical pedigree, comparing it to the Aristotelians who thought God too happy in himself to attend to mortals
Calvin declines to choose between the two charges and joins them, making prosperity itself the cause of the hardening
themes: A candle carried into the secret cells
Wine left standing until it turns harsh
A God supposed too happy to look down
Houses built for someone else to live in

14.pericope_label: The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly
debates: Whether the day meant is the coming invasion or the last judgment
Why the nearness is repeated
Whose voice is heard in the day of the Lord
outliers: Ellicott identifies the voice as the cry of a baffled warrior who can neither fight nor flee
Clarke fixes the day between the death of Josiah at Megiddo and the fall of the city
themes: A cry of fire raised at the next door
A day flying faster than time itself
Strong men crying for fear as children do
Darkness borrowed from a mountain of revelation

16.pericope_label: A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high towers
debates: Who is the real commander of the invading army
What the blindness of the men describes
Whether the closing word means speed or thoroughness
outliers: Calvin objects to the received rendering of the last noun and reads a full end rather than a riddance
Gill identifies the hoarded silver as the very lees the secure men were settled on
themes: A trumpet blown at last in triumph
Wise men given blindness to match their wisdom
Blood spilt as carelessly as dust in a road
Gold heaped into mountains that turn nothing aside
